#1726. Manchester United players will need a slap if they agree with Gary Neville relegation prediction

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

#1722. Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard accuses Mauricio Pochettino of disrespecting Man Utd star

Steven Gerrard fears Mauricio Pochettino is already on collision course with one of his senior Manchester United players following Sunday’s damaging 4-0 defeat against Liverpool.

Any hope of a new manager bounce was extinguished during a frantic opening quarter of an hour at Anfield yesterday when the hosts roared into a two goal lead following Leny Yoro’s sending off.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled on the agony in the closing stages and ensured the scoreline gave a more accurate representation of Liverpool’s near total dominance.

While playing the entire match at a numerical disadvantage certainly played a role in the one-sided nature of such an eagerly anticipated contest, United were second best from the off and were made to pay for their new manager’s questionable team selection.

The decision to drop Harry Maguire at the expense of Matthijs de Ligt, who is still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was questioned by the likes of Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville before kick-off and their skepticism was vindicated when the Dutch centre-half played a role in Yoro’s red card.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Gerrard, meanwhile, went a step further in his criticism by accusing Pochettino of showing a lack of respect to Maguire by relegating him to the bench in his first game at the helm.

‘I thought he got it wrong,’ Gerrard told The Overlap with Sky Bet. ‘I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone in a game of that magnitude, it’s the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world.

‘To play someone that hadn’t played since last November. You can understand the manager wanting to come in and put his stamp on it and change a few things that had been going on previously, but Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment.

‘Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt’s been out for a year. Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game.

‘And he made a difference when he came on. And he was one who was putting his body on the line. He made a great block, I think it was around the 38th, 39th minute, which stopped a certain goal. And I’ve watched Manchester United a lot this season, and he’s one who’s having a go.

‘He’s one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn’t been perfect, but to not play him and put de Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful.’

#1721. Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026

Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

By this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later said. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’

Arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

So dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

Arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ said Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

The league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

At least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

Come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

Newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90)

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

The punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

So, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ said Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’

Newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

#1720. Amorim proud of ‘intelligent, courageous’ Milan, world-class Rabiot and Ramos

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was important that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team showed the levels that they are capable of.

Now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it showed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

“We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

“I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

“I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”

“The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

“Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

“Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an important objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

“Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”

#1719. Burnley vs Birmingham City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 23 Nov 2026 17:51

Still searching for that elusive home league victory, Burnley welcome Birmingham City to Turf Moor for a Championship battle on Wednesday night.

The Clarets shared the spoils in the East Lancashire derby against Blackburn Rovers on the weekend, whilst Blues were bested in a top-of-the-table clash by Stoke City in Staffordshire.

Burnley's winless run in the Championship extended to seven matches (D3 L4) due to a 2-2 draw with rivals Blackburn on Sunday afternoon, after which defender Kyle Walker conceded that his side were in a relegation battle.

Goals either side of the half-time whistle from Largie Ramazani and Jaydon Banel were not enough to claim maximum points at the expense of Rovers, with the Clarets last winning a home league fixture in October 2025.

Winning just one of their opening 16 second-tier fixtures of the campaign, Burnley are currently occupying 22nd position in the Championship rankings, four points from the safety of managerless Watford in 21st place.

As alluded to earlier, the Clarets are the only side in the division who are yet to enjoy a victory in front of their home faithful, with Wednesday's hosts drawing six and losing two of their eight Turf Moor clashes.

The October arrival of Swiss manager Fabio Celestini to replace Nicky Hayen has failed to get Burnley on the winning track, with the 51-year-old enduring a four-game winless run (D3 L1) at the beginning of his Lancashire tenure.

Following three straight consecutive Championship wins, Birmingham City spent the November international break at the very summit of the second-tier rankings, however, Saturday's defeat by Stoke knocked Chris Davies's side off their perch.

In the end, a second-half strike from former Ipswich Town marksman George Hirst was enough to beat Blues, who failed to take advantage of a numerical advantage after Luca Bombino's 63rd-minute dismissal.

Despite the weekend's loss at the bet365 Stadium, Birmingham have made an exceptional start to the 2026-27 campaign and sit in fourth place in the Championship standings, three points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

Davies's troops are much-improved on their travels compared to last term, however, the Second City club have lost two of their past three away contests, including a trip to Cardiff City (0-1) in October.

Given Burnley's success in the Championship over the past decade or so, it is no surprise that Birmingham are six games without a win in this matchup (W3 D3), last defeating the Clarets at Turf Moor in January 2013, when Marlon King netted a 90th-minute winner.

Picking up a straight red card in the 5-4 defeat by Cardiff at the start of the month, Burnley's Connor Roberts remains unavailable this week.

The Clarets have a number of attacking options on the sidelines, including Armando Broja, Ashley Barnes and Dastan Satpaev.

Birmingham are sweating over the fitness of Jhon Solis, with the Colombia international missing the loss at Stoke on Saturday.

The former Girona man would be a major miss at Turf Moor, where Blues might field Paik Seung-Ho alongside Tomoki Iwata in the midfield once again.

Collecting his fifth yellow card of the season last time out, captain Christoph Klarer is suspended and should be replaced by Dael Fry at centre-back.

Weiss; Walker, Alleyne, Julio, Sonne; Hatate, Cullen, Laurent; Ramazani, Edwards, Amdouni

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:

Allsop; Osayi-Samuel, Neumann, Fry, Cochrane; Iwata, Paik; Vicente, Stansfield, Millar; Priske

Without a home league victory in over 13 months, Burnley are low on confidence despite a recent managerial alteration.

Birmingham are not the same beast without Solis but should be good enough for at least a point at Turf Moor.

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:02

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that struggling Brazilian superstar Vinicius Junior will "return to his full potential".

The 26-year-old signed a new mega-money deal with Real Madrid over the summer after rejecting the chance to make the move to Arsenal.

However, it has been a tough campaign for the attacker, who has only come up with one goal and three assists in 13 appearances for the club.

Vinicius was left out of the starting XI against Celta Vigo in the league on Saturday, instead featuring as a second-half substitute in his side's 2-1 success.

Mourinho has confirmed that the forward will be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, and the Portuguese remains convinced that the South American will soon return to his highest level for Los Blancos.

“He’ll return to his full potential. He’s young, and sometimes when players approach or pass the age of 30, they struggle to maintain their ideal physical condition and some lose a bit of their motivation," Mourinho told reporters during Monday's press conference.

"Vini Jr. is young, and people can forget that he arrived very young and reached an extremely high level far too soon. He’s won everything, but when people were out to get him, he always said he’s a really good lad and very empathetic towards everyone.

"That’s a fundamental foundation. He had a very positive impact the other day and I remember that against Villarreal he turned the game around, but he was out for four matches due to his sending-off and that disrupted his development and his confidence. At the weekend he came on well and helped turn the match around.

“He’s playing tomorrow and we’re all hoping to see him at his best. I saw him last season, but on the other side, with Benfica dominating and the Bernabeu silent. A goal from Vini Jr. and the tie was over.

"That’s the Vini Jr. we want, but as far as I’m concerned there’s no pressure – he just needs to keep working hard as he’s been doing and help the team in attack and with defensive organisation. If he gives his all alongside me, he doesn’t need to be the man of the match.”

Vinicius has been named in the squad for Real Madrid's European clash with PSV on Tuesday, but Endrick, Rodrygo, Raul Asencio and Ferland Mendy are out due to injuries.

Denzel Dumfries missed training on Monday and was regarded as a doubt, but the Netherlands international has been named in the squad.

“For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”

#1711. Chelsea star reveals he ‘considered retirement’ under Enzo Maresca: ‘I wasn’t happy anymore’

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Wesley Fofana has revealed he almost quit football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge of Chelsea.

The French centre-back says he considered retiring early due to the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries.

Fofana, 25, did continue playing and is starting regularly this season for Chelsea, but has been much criticised in recent weeks for his performances under Xabi Alonso, including in Saturday’s 4-1 home defeat to Leeds.

“There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries,” Fofana said.

“Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.

“I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.

“I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’”

Fofana, speaking in an interview with Zack Nani TV, continued: “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’

“They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made. Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you’re injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.’

“But at that moment, I really felt that the pain football caused me far outweighed the joy, so why continue? I was in pain almost 100 per cent of the time. Every time I gritted my teeth, played a few games, and just started to find a little love and joy in life again, bang, I’d get injured again.”

The Red Devils would also not have to break the bank to sign Toney, with a loan deal a very attractive proposition, and Mauricio Pochettino's side should not pass up the chance to do what could be a very successful piece of January business.

#1707. How the Dylan Tombides Foundation is educating footballers about testicular cancer

15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer. He would pass away three years later at the age of 20.

Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.

Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.

That is why the DT38 Foundation was set up in Dylan’s name and why Tracy and Taylor, in partnership with FIFA Medical, are explaining to players at this year’s U17 World Cup in Doha why regular self-examination matters and how to carry it out.

“Getting the call from FIFA was a massive opportunity and an amazing thing for us and for the charity,” Taylor tells Standard Sport.

“Obviously, it’s where Dylan last kind of played healthy before his diagnosis. So to come back to where it all started for us as a family is a grateful honour.”

£75m Chelsea star ‘considered retirement’ under Maresca

Fernandes fumes in unseen interview amid new Man Utd red card verdict

Chelsea injury update: Caicedo, Joao Pedro, James latest return dates

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

Tracy and Taylor have spoken to more than 1,200 players across the tournament, and their story has really hit home.

“One of the young players stood in front of me and said, ‘I’m so sorry for your loss. I’m sorry your son isn’t coming home to you. We are so grateful that you are telling us all about it’,” Tracy says.

“(We are) very grateful to have this opportunity to educate 1,200 players out here this fortnight, that hopefully will go home and pass on the message of the signs and symptoms of testicular cancer and the importance of an ultrasound scan.”

The DT38 foundation have a campaign called ‘Check One Two’, encouraging men to check themselves on the first day of every month.

Dylan’s nickname - ‘Didge’ - also provides an acronym and hashtag for the foundation: Delay Is Deadly, Get Educated.

FIFA medical director Andy Massey has worked with the DT38 Foundation to get Tracy and Taylor talking to players at the U17 World Cup and says it is an initiative that he hopes to continue year on year.

“What I would love to do is carry this on next year for the Under-17s,” Massey says.

“It’s an annual event now (the World Cup) for Under-17s. We’re going to be in the same place until 2029, and it would be fantastic to do it (talk to players) again for next year and the year after.”

We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it

Massey continued by underlining the value of the work Tracy and Taylor are doing, with free scans now on offer to players during the tournament.

“We don’t want this to be a box-ticking exercise. We don’t want this to be a, ‘Let’s pat ourselves on the back, we’re working for a charity’.

“This is one of the biggest things that I think I’ve ever done in my sports medicine career because it has such a reach.”

The DT38 Foundation are starting with the U17 World Cup, but ultimately Taylor hopes their work will have an impact down the generations.

“The effect is lasting,” he says. “If we can teach these kids now, we know the next generation, they’ll teach their kids and they’ll teach their kids and it’ll be continuous.

“We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it. Without FIFA, we couldn’t touch as many people as we have.”

Visit dt38.org to find out more about the DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole said of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has cast doubt on his future, four months into his first full season at Tottenham Hotspur.

The Italian joined Spurs shortly thereafter with the club one point away from a first relegation since 1977, and clinched Premier League survival with final-day delight against David Moyes’ Everton.

Currently sat in 10th place, De Zerbi’s Spurs are targeting a weekend victory against relegation-threatened Sunderland to continue a run of good form, but the manager has his eyes set on more.

He said: “I don’t measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have.

#1703. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino to use USA connection to help Red Devils 'land' defensive upgrade in January

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:38, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:41

Manchester United are reportedly planning to make a move for Villarreal defender Alex Freeman when the January transfer window opens for business.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

Man United are expected to be busy during the winter market, with at least one defender likely to arrive, while the club are also said to be planning to sign a striker.

Centre-back has been a major problem for the 20-time English champions this season, but right-back is also an issue, with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui having tough campaigns.

According to Football Insider, Man United are planning to bring a new right-back to Old Trafford in January in the shape of Villarreal's Freeman.

The report claims that Man United scouts have been impressed by Freeman's level since he made the move to European football with Villarreal.

Freeman is well-known to new Red Devils head coach Mauricio Pochettino following their time together with the USA; the 22-year-old has 28 caps for his national team, scoring three goals and registering three assists in the process.

"There will be players in that US national team that Pochettino will be a big fan of," journalist Pete O'Rourke said on the Transfer Insider podcast.

"If he feels any player from that squad that can come in and improve the Manchester United side, then that is something he'd be foolish not to look at as well.

"There's been talk of Alex Freeman the full-back from Villarreal as being a potential target, after he has been outstanding playing in Spain.

"Obviously defence is going to be a top priority for United over the next couple of transfer windows to try and reshape the squad, and Pochettino could be key to that deal."

Freeman started his professional career with Orlando City, making 42 appearances for the club, scoring six goals and registering seven assists, ahead of a move to Villarreal in January 2026.

The defender has one goal in 26 appearances for Villarreal, including four outings in the Champions League, while he has netted once in 17 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season.

Freeman has a contract with Villarreal until the summer of 2032.

#1702. KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

In Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park

Frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’

Frick shows his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to quickly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

For the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

If Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game

Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall showed him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann said: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really big, big chances, and we don't take them.

‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’

#1701. Rabiot reveals belief Milan are ‘growing’ and commends Ramos: “Not everyone understands”

Adrien Rabiot heaped praise on Goncalo Ramos for what he does for the team, but he also explained what AC Milan’s ‘problem’ is.

Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1. Gabriele Calvani’s own goal put the home side ahead, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted to make it a rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is a third consecutive league victory after the wins over Inter and Genoa and it moves the Rossoneri on to 27 points, back inside the Champions League places. Up next: a trip to Athens to face Olympiacos on Thursday in the Europa League, and a chance to demonstrate consistency.

After the full-time whistle, Rabiot spoke alongside Ramos to both Sky and DAZN, offering his thoughts on what was a very successful evening in front of all the fans at San Siro. His words are via MilanNews.

Are you starting to build a good identity?

“Our problem is that we have to be focused for 90 minutes. We did well today, even though we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. As I said, we’re growing as a team: the quality of our play, the team spirit, the sacrifice for 90 minutes, and everyone.

“Gonçalo is the first to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of games: I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit. But everyone’s attitude was great today, and we have to keep it up.

“In these last few games, when we play like this, when we’re so focused and manage to do what we work towards in training, I think we’re all enjoying ourselves, even tonight. We created a lot, we scored a lot of goals. What we have to focus on is enjoying playing together.”

Why didn’t you shoot before the first goal?

“I wanted Pulisic to score, but the defender came back quickly. It’s true that I could have shot, but I get more pleasure from providing an assist than from scoring. But I did the assist afterwards.”

“He does a great job. Not everyone understands it, but he does an incredible job. When we get in and score, it’s also credit to us. Then we feel happy when he scores, also because it gives him confidence. Good for us and for him, for everyone.”

#1698. Atletico Madrid vs Viking FK - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 19:14, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:42

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to return to winning ways in the Champions League when they continue their league stage campaign against Viking FK on Wednesday night.

This match will represent the first-ever contest between Atletico and Viking, although the Spanish team have won six of their seven previous meetings against Norwegian clubs.

Atletico boast a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's Champions League league stage, with the result leaving them 23rd in the overall table on four points.

Diego Simeone's side opened their league stage campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool before beating Manchester United and then drawing with Stuttgart, but they suffered a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich in their last fixture in the competition.

Atletico have European games against PSV Eindhoven, Bodo/Glimt and Fenerbahce to come after this one, and it would be a major shock if they were not present in the knockout round of the tournament.

The Red and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight, with the result leaving them third in the La Liga table on 31 points, five points behind leaders Barcelona.

Atletico lost 2-1 on aggregate to Arsenal in last season's Champions League semi-finals, and they have been runners-up in this tournament on two occasions (2014 and 2016).

Viking, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's league stage, and they actually sit above Atletico in the table (22nd).

The Eliteserien champions lost their section opener to Stuttgart before claiming a point in a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich, but they were then beaten by Aston Villa at Villa Park.

The Dark Blues did have a huge European win last time out, though, recording a 4-1 victory over Sabah, which gave their hopes of qualification a huge boost.

Viking, who are jointly-managed by Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen, are playing in the Champions League for the first time since 1992-93, when they were beaten by Barcelona in the first round.

The Norwegian outfit have scored in their last 12 European matches, which is a club record, while none of Atletico's last 42 Champions League fixtures have finished goalless.

Atletico will be without the services of Ademola Lookman (knee), Marc Pubill (ankle) and Cristian Romero (muscular) for the Champions League fixture with Viking.

Lee Kang-in could be introduced into the starting side on Wednesday, with the 25-year-old potentially featuring alongside Julian Alvarez in the final third of the field.

Alex Baena is set to continue down the left off the back of his excellent performance against Getafe, while Johnny Cardoso is likely to feature in the middle of the midfield.

As for Viking, Anders Baertelsen (foot), Sondre Bjorshol (knee), Nick D'Agostino (leg) and Martin Ove Roseth (muscular) are out of the match due to injury problems.

Meanwhile, Veton Berisha (unspecified) and Kristoffer Haugen (unspecified) both need to be assessed before final decisions on their availability can be made.

Peter Christiansen is the team's leading goalscorer this season with 19, and the 26-year-old will once again feature in the final third of the field.

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Simeone, Barrios, Cardoso, Baena; Kang-in, Alvarez

Ostbo; Heggheim, Stensness, Falchener, Auklend; Bjordal, Bell, Askildsen; Christiansen, Botheim, Tripic

Viking have enough quality to find the back of the net against Atletico, but we are fully expecting Simeone's side to secure a valuable three points in the Champions League.

#1694. Hibernian vs Dundee - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 23 Nov 2026 19:39, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 19:39

Hibernian FC host Dundee FC in the Scottish Premiership at Easter Road Stadium on Tuesday.

The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.

Marink Reedijk's Hibernian sit 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 11 points from 13 games, a return of three wins, two draws and eight defeats, and their goal difference of minus six is the product of 15 goals scored and 21 conceded.

The Hibees are the only club in the division yet to win a league match at home this season, and they have conceded 15 goals in seven league games at Easter Road.

Dundee United made that record worse on Saturday, with Zac Sapsford scoring from the rebound after Raphael Sallinger saved his sixth-minute penalty, adding a second before half time, and Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall completing a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's heaviest home defeat to United.

Reedijk was appointed on September 24 after David Gray was sacked, and he lost his first three league games in charge, 1-0 at Dundee United on October 10 and 2-1 at home to both Falkirk on October 17 and Celtic on October 25.

The cup has been kinder, as goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath beat Heart of Midlothian 2-1 at Hampden Park on November 1, Hibernian's first win over their city rivals at the national stadium after four defeats there, and set up a Premier Sports Cup final against Rangers on Sunday, December 13.

McGrath then struck a 25-yard shot just before the hour at Pittodrie on November 7, and substitutes Callum Wright, Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added the rest in a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's biggest at Aberdeen since 1968 and remains Reedijk's only league victory.

Joe Newell, who wore the captain's armband against United in place of the injured Felix Passlack, spoke afterwards of the players' shame and embarrassment, and the midfielder will know that Tuesday offers the first chance to answer it in front of the Easter Road crowd.

Steven Pressley's Dundee sit seventh with 17 points from 13 games, a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats that leaves them six points and four places above Hibernian, with 18 goals scored and 23 conceded.

The Dee had conceded only 15 times in their first 12 league games and collected five wins in that run, with Owen Goodman playing every minute in goal and keeping two clean sheets.

That solidity vanished on Saturday, when Hearts led 4-0 at half time and Owen Bevan was sent off on 56 minutes for a foul on Claudio Braga, with the visitors winning 8-0 in what The Courier described as Dundee's worst-ever defeat at Dens Park.

Pressley took responsibility for the display afterwards, while pundit Richard Foster argued the players must also own a result that was Hearts' biggest top-flight win since 1957.

The defeat came a fortnight after a 2-1 loss at St Johnstone on November 7, and it ended an unbeaten home run of four league games for a side that had collected the bulk of its points at Dens Park.

Dundee will also remember that Hibernian won the first meeting 2-1 at Dens Park on August 30, and Tuesday is the second of three league games between the sides before the split.

Bradley Fink and Joe Westley share the Dundee scoring lead with four league goals each, and Westley, who takes the penalties, came off the bench to equalise at St Johnstone within two minutes of the restart.

Passlack, who took the captaincy from Boyle after Reedijk's arrival, is out with a hamstring injury sustained in the eighth minute at Aberdeen, and Reedijk has refused to put a date on his return as the defender races to be fit for the Rangers final.

Alex Williams replaced Passlack at Pittodrie and made his first start against United, so he is the likely right-back again.

Grant Hanley is out after thumb surgery, Adam Mayor has a hamstring problem, and on-loan Stoke City striker Nathan Lowe has a stress fracture that Reedijk will assess week by week.

Kanayo Megwa remains sidelined with a thigh problem and Rocky Bushiri is still recovering from the Achilles injury he suffered in May.

Left-back Jordan Obita is back in contention after a calf injury, and on-loan Manchester United midfielder Jacob Devaney returned from international duty with Ireland, giving Reedijk extra options if he rings the changes.

Owen Elding, 20, leads the line in Lowe's absence, with Boyle and McGrath operating around him as they did in the Hampden semi-final.

For the visitors, Bevan serves the first of a two-match ban after his straight red card against Hearts, ruling him out at Easter Road and at Aberdeen on Saturday, November 28.

Joe Wright, who was on the bench against Hearts, is the natural replacement alongside Ryan Astley, but he has played little league football this season.

Simon Murray, Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse are all out for the season with anterior cruciate ligament injuries.

Bobby Wales, the on-loan striker, is still recovering from an ankle injury.

Goodman, beaten eight times at Dens Park, is expected to keep his place in goal.

#1688. Who is Piero Ausilio? Tottenham’s reported new target to be sporting director

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have been linked to Piero Ausilio, with the former Inter Milan sporting director earmarked for a similar role at the Premier League club.

Italian outlet Tuttosport report that Spurs are closing in on a deal to bring Ausilio to north London.

It is hoped that Ausilio could be installed in time to take charge of Spurs’ transfer approach for the January transfer window.

Tottenham’s executive structure has frequently changed since 2023.

Fabio Paratici joined the club in 2021 as sporting director, but stepped down in April 2023 ahead of a 30-month ban from all football activities handed to him by FIFA after a conviction for financial malpractice.

Paratici returned to his role in October 2025 after the conclusion of his suspension, sharing duties with co-sporting director Johan Lange.

But his return did not last long, as Paratici quit Spurs in February of this year, meaning Lange stepped up to become sole sporting director.

Ausilio ended a 28-year association with Inter Milan in the summer, with the Italian giants deciding not to renew his contract as sporting director.

Initially joining the club’s youth academy in 1998, Ausilio worked his way through the ranks to become sporting director in 2014.

Midway through his first season in his role, Ausilio was named as the TMW award’s best sporting director at the start of 2015. In 2024 Ausilio was recognised as the ‘best sporting director’ in football at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Retiring from football after injury as a teenager, Ausilio holds a degree in law, having studied at the University of Milan.

Over the years Ausilio has garnered a strong reputation for his scouting and squad-building, helping to construct a team at the San Siro that has won three Serie A titles and reached the Champions League final twice in the past five seasons.

#1687. GdS: ‘Turbo Milan’ – how Frosinone were dismantled by five-star counter-attacking display

AC Milan put in one of their best performances under Ruben Amorim so far to sweep aside Frosinone at San Siro.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by writing that Lazio, Roma and Juventus also had fun this weekend, scoring a flurry of goals in their victories, but it is Milan that might just come away from the round 12 feeling best.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

It was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

The Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

There was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

Yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

All this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

It might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

Keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

Just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

It paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

There were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

The end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

They’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Bruno Guimaraes has revealed the one piece of advice Declan Rice gave him that helped him settle after joining Arsenal.

The Brazilian midfielder sealed an acrimonious move from Newcastle to north London in August after an extended transfer saga, and had fresh silverware to his name almost immediately after beating Manchester City in the Community Shield.

#1684. New system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

There were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

But the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel issues in January but they currently sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

New boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat

Anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

That is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant issue.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

The Coventry boss said: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’

Cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

“I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

#1680. Crystal Palace handed WSL points deduction after illegal substitution as relegation worries intensify

Women’s Super League strugglers Crystal Palace have been handed a three-point deduction after breaching substitution rules against Everton in September.

Palace opened their WSL campaign with a 1-0 victory over the Toffees thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first-half goal.

But they will not be able to keep hold of their points haul from that victory, having made use of a fourth substitution window in second-half injury time, when only three are permitted per match.

That saw them introduce Kirsty Howat in place of Shannon O’Brien in the seventh of eight added minutes.

A statement from the WSL confirms Crystal Palace admitted their breach of competition rules, while an independent tribunal dubbed the move “inadvertent” and “not intended to secure an unfair advantage”. It also acknowledged Palace have taken steps to ensure the incident would not be repeated.

However, it maintained a sporting sanction would be necessary, writing: “The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained.”

Howat did not touch the ball in her time on the pitch, which lasted less than one minute, though Everton maintained her introduction handed the Eagles an unfair advantage. The tribunal concurred, adding in their decision that Howat’s lack of influence on the match did not amount to “exceptional circumstances.”

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

The imposed three-point deduction will leave Palace on six points with 11 matches played and drop them to 11th place in the table, above only winless Charlton Athletic. Should they finish the season in that position, they would face a play-off with the WSL2’s second-place finisher for their place in the top flight.

Palace said in a club statement that they are “disappointed” by the tribunal’s decision, adding they feel they have been stripped of a “deserved victory.”

The statement read: “Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.”

Palace do not have the option to appeal the tribunal’s decision.

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 20:00

Former Tottenham Hotspur striker Darren Bent, in an exclusive interview with Sports Mole, has revealed his 'shock' at Richarlison still being at the club ahead of the January transfer window.

The Brazil international has gone from finishing the 2025-26 season as Spurs' top scorer to being completely ostracised from the group under Roberto De Zerbi following his vocal desire to leave the club.

Richarlison featured in Tottenham's season opener against Brentford but has not been involved in a senior squad since, only making one appearance for the Under-21s in an EFL Trophy loss to Cheltenham Town.

Tottenham plan to sell Richarlison in January, but they will reportedly refuse to sanction his exit to a Premier League rival, opening the door for either Trabzonspor or Galatasaray to make a move.

In the meantime, the 29-year-old will simply continue to maintain his fitness levels at Hotspur Way, but ex-Spurs forward Bent is amazed that the Lilywhites did not cut him from their ranks during the summer.

"Because he was so vocal about wanting to leave, I just think they were always going to clash," Bent said. "I felt De Zerbi and Richarlison, because of their big personalities, were always going to clash.

"I know with Richarlison, although he was their top goalscorer last season, and it's going to sound a bit strange saying it coming from a centre-forward, but it just felt like it was a bit of a, not quite the best of a bad bunch, but there was no consistency to him.

"Someone had to step up and score the goals, and Richarlison did that. But week on week, you could never really count on him in terms of stepping up and scoring the goals consistently.

"So I understand why De Zerbi opted to not have him in the squad and tried other options. I'm just shocked he's still there. I thought they would have sent him out on loan or at least sold him just to get him out there, because when they want to sell him now, he's obviously spent a lot of time not playing. He needs to be playing games. I can't see this relationship going on for too much longer."

After scoring 12 goals in all competitions during the 2025-26 season - 11 of which came in the Premier League - Richarlison told De Zerbi that he wanted to explore a transfer away, but such a move failed to materialise in the summer.

In the last knockings of the transfer window, Tottenham were advancing in talks with Everton over separate deals for Richarlison and Iliman Ndiaye, but the Brazilian ultimately refused to re-join his old club.

After the European windows closed, Richarlison was heavily linked with Brazilian outfit Vasco da Gama, but that proposed transfer also collapsed, apparently due to disagreements on personal terms.

The ex-Watford man is then understood to have explored terminating his Tottenham contract, but he remains tied to the Lilywhites until at least January for the time being.

Now, Spurs have supposedly slapped an asking price of just £10m on the head of Richarlison, meaning that they are willing to accept a £40m loss on the player they signed for £50m in 2022.

Richarlison has scored 32 goals and provided 15 assists in 134 outings for Tottenham in all competitions.

#1676. Senegal awarded Afcon 2025 title by CAS verdict as Morocco stripped

Senegal have been confirmed as champions of AFCON 2025 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld their appeal, bringing an end to an ugly months-long saga.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In March 2026, two months after the final, CAF announced the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch. The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco.

Senegal then appealed the decision at CAS, and have now been reinstated as champions after it was confirmed their appeal was upheld.

Man Utd fans tell Mbeumo to ‘go to sleep’ after posting GTA 6 photo

Pochettino learns size of Man Utd transfer budget as targets revealed

Crystal Palace handed WSL points deduction after illegal substitution

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

A statement from CAS read: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).”

A decision shared in a press release on Tuesday explained: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.”

The panel decided that Articles 82 and 84 of the tournament rules, which formed the basis of Morocco’s appeal, were only applicable when a referee was forced to permanently call off a match. Given he allowed the match to restart and finish, those articles were no longer considered applicable.

“In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,” the court press release continued.

“The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as ‘arbitrary’. On the contrary, the referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”

United are just one point ahead of bottom club Crystal Palace. It is hard to know whether the answer will come through the January window, but the United hierarchy could think so.

Evanilson, 27, has scored eight goals and provided five assists in 15 games this season. He said: ‘Here in England, among the big clubs, Manchester United are the team I like most. Rayan said the same. When I was a kid, I used to watch United too. When Cristiano Ronaldo played there, I watched loads of his highlights. And, man, knowing that I am here playing against them... This is my third season playing against them. I scored last season and I scored this season at Old Trafford. It is a dream, and I say it to everyone in interviews: it was a dream to play in that stadium, and scoring goals is even more important. So it is a dream I am fulfilling, scoring a goal against United because of the greatness of the club.’

With a contract until June 2029, Evanilson is unlikely to leave Bournemouth in the middle of the season. The club, fifth in the table, probably have no intention of letting their number nine go, as he is their top scorer and assist provider in the Premier League. The chance of securing European football could encourage Bournemouth to ignore any offer from United.

For their part, there is no specific rumour suggesting United are interested in the forward, but the club’s poor sporting situation opens the door to a larger recruitment drive in January. With striker Benjamin Sesko injured, United are thinking about Pio Esposito, who is in great form for Inter Milan. And why not try Evanilson, who is already a fan of the Red Devils and could well be tempted by the prospect of moving despite everything?
