#1673. Senegal reinstated as 2025 AFCON champions

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Senegal have been reinstated as the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) ruling.

The decision overturns a previous decision to strip Senegal of the title they won against hosts Morocco during a chaotic showpiece match in January.

The Teranga Lions triumphed 1-0 in the final after extra time, with Pape Gueye's 94th-minute goal; however, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations during the match.

Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest of a penalty awarded against them before then returning to the field – Brahim Diaz went on to miss that spot-kick, forcing extra time.

The decision to give Morocco the title came two months after the final, but Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to CAS, which backed the decision of referee Jean-Jacques Ndala.

Ndala opted to restart the game after Senegal returned to the pitch, and the match was played to its conclusion, meaning the result of the final stands, and they have been confirmed as the AFCON 2025 winners.

/ on dit quoi!!!! https://t.co/S1NY98nhf1

— Football Senegal (@FootballSenegal) November 24, 2026

"The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025)," a CAS statement read.

"The decision rendered by the CAF appeal board is set aside, and the decision by the CAF disciplinary board is reinstated.

"Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal)."

It means that Senegal have won their last two AFCON finals (2021 and 2025), after losing their first two (2002 and 2019).

That match also marked the first time Senegal had scored a goal in an AFCON final (fourth appearance), with Gueye's goal also the nation's 100th at the tournament.

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

Milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

Corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Wesley Fofana has laughed off his penalty miss that sent Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup in an interview that could complicate his relationship with an already disappointed fanbase.

Fofana was part of a Chelsea defence that has lost 1-0 to Sunderland and 4-1 at home to Leeds in the Blues’ last two games as Xabi Alonso’s side struggle for form in the Premier League.

The 25-year-old Fofana has conducted a two-and-a-half-hour interview with Zack Nani TV in which he admitted he almost quit football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge of Chelsea due to regular long-term injury setbacks.

But in the interview, which it is understood was not arranged by the club, Fofana also spoke about missing the decisive penalty in the shootout as Chelsea were eliminated by Liverpool from the Carabao Cup last month at Anfield. The manner in which he discussed his miss threatens to irk some supporters.

“The Liverpool match was tough to take, but I moved on quickly because that’s just part of football,” Fofana said.

“I took responsibility for the penalty - I missed it - and, well, I knew I wasn’t a good penalty taker to begin with, you know [laughs]?”

Fofana continued: “So, I just thought, ‘Okay, I’ll own it.’ But I ended up conceding a penalty during the match - it was a handball - but that’s just part of the game. I could have avoided it; it’s the kind of thing we talk about - you have to be consistent, and you have to keep improving in those areas.

“But after the penalty, I stepped up, because I’m one of the most experienced players. Out on the field, there were a lot of young guys. And, well, you had to get out there, you know?

#1670. Manchester United learn Leny Yoro red card appeal verdict after controversial suspension

Leny Yoro will be available for Manchester United’s Premier League meeting with Brentford this weekend after his one-match suspension was struck off on appeal.

The centre-back was dismissed after just eight minutes as United visited Liverpool on Sunday for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak.

The Swede was through one-on-one with Senne Lammens and took a heavy first touch before being caught by the backtracking Yoro, just outside the box. Dominik Szoboszlai scored the opener from the resultant free-kick and United ultimately lost 4-0.

United were quick to appeal the decision, which new head coach Mauricio Pochettino and a number of his players questioned in post-match media duties.

And their appeal has been upheld, meaning Yoro will be available this weekend for the visit of Brentford to Old Trafford.

A statement from the FA read: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal. The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”

Speaking post-match, United captain Fernandes questioned the decision to send Yoro off, saying Isak drew the foul and was not in control of the ball anyway.

“We have four officials at the game, plus another two on VAR. I understand it’s a difficult situation, but VAR can watch it again and again, with replays, slow motion, everything,” he told ESPN Brasil.

“Isak puts his leg in front of Leny simply to try to win a foul. The ball is knocked forward, towards Senne’s hands. He has absolutely no control of the ball.

“For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”

Pochettino echoed his complaints, adding: “The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”

#1669. How Noni Madueke grew into a unique piece at Arsenal amid injury absences

By Alexis Pereira | 23 Nov 2026 21:02

Noni Madueke’s signing for Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had played a game. Signed from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing, and he had to justify an investment in a player who initially appeared destined to be a back-up.

A little more than a year later, the discussion is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke received a longer run of opportunities and took the space. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of that growth.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In his press conference, the boss highlighted the variety the forward has added to the game and his involvement without the ball.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives in one-on-one situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In 2024-25, he was one of the Premier League players who progressed the ball towards the box the most and created danger mainly through individual carries. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

‘He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forwards,’ Arteta said. ‘And he is doing it in various ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and much more connection to his game.’

The numbers help show the scale of the growth. According to FotMob’s Premier League 2026-27 data, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, against 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although Saka has played fewer minutes. The growth also shows in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

‘And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball,’ Arteta said. ‘So I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying that a lot.’

The development is therefore not about abandoning the dribble, but knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, but now seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

Comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right and move inside, but they do it in different ways. Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and moves naturally between carries, short passes and crosses. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal’s main attacking tools.

Madueke offers more explosion in the first movement and tends to seek one-on-one duels more often. He is more vertical, liking to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When confident, he can disorganise a defence without relying on a long build-up.

The creation data help illustrate the difference. As well as beating Saka for chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob’s numbers, Madueke also shows a higher volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps an advantage in shooting and defensive involvement. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

That difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka may be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that breaks down the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating individual imbalances.

The Englishman has also shown he can play on the left, a role he took on when Christos Tzolis was absent. There he must adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can go to the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta’s options and stops the team depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka does not need to be seen as an attempt to remove the starter. Arsenal need more than one player able to decide matches, especially in a long season with the Premier League, Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is beginning to offer arguments to be considered more than simple cover.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player’s reaction as an example to the rest of the squad. The boss said Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

‘He went to train and came back a different Noni,’ Arteta explained. ‘He was not willing to accept that situation and showed he was determined. Since then, it has been incredible.’

The individual work did not start now, however. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has worked for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention on being more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown in the numbers: his average of chances created more than doubled compared with the previous season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate rose from 50 per cent to 55 per cent, while his pass accuracy went from 78 per cent to 87 per cent. In open-play crosses, his success rate jumped from 14 per cent to 33 per cent.

Those numbers help explain why Arteta speaks of a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but has begun to execute other actions better, which could previously limit his influence. The growth combined different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

#1666. MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up big-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

An initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

#1665. Palace docked three points for substitution rule breach in Everton victory

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points for breaching substitution rules during their 1-0 win over Everton on the opening day of the Women's Super League.

Lexi Lloyd-Smith scored the only goal at The 360 Engage Stadium in September, but the Eagles have since had those points removed after using too many substitution windows.

The introduction of Kirsty Howat in the 97th minute was Palace's fourth separate change, with other substitutions taking place in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time-wasting.

An independent tribunal determined that the breach was "inadvertent" and that it was "not intended to secure an unfair advantage," but added that a sporting sanction was "necessary."

The deduction means Palace drop to 13th in the WSL and behind Birmingham City on goal difference, after the Eagles were thumped 5-1 by London City Lionesses on Sunday.

Crystal Palace have been informed of the decision by a panel to agree to the WSL’s recommendation to deduct three points from our 2026/27 Barclays Women’s Super League tally, following the 97th-minute substitution that used a ‘fourth’ window in our recent fixture against Everton. https://t.co/aNpga6nt4C

— Crystal Palace F.C. Women (@cpfc_w) November 24, 2026

The Everton match was one of only two WSL games Palace had won this season, and the Eagles said they were "disappointed" by the outcome.

"Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate," Palace's statement read.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

#1664. Brentford 4-0 Everton: Keane Lewis-Potter takes Bees to Premier League goalscoring milestone in dominant win

By Ben Sully | 23 Nov 2026 23:01, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 03:42

Brentford scored their 300th Premier League goal in Monday's commanding 4-0 Premier League win over Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted a quickfire brace to put the Bees in control, before their position was strengthened further by James Tarkowski's 40th-minute red card for a challenge that was deemed dangerous after a VAR review.

In the second half, Vitaly Janelt produced a stunning long-range effort, and Fabio Carvalho netted his second league goal of the season to seal back-to-back home wins.

Not only did they claim an impressive victory, but the Bees also hit a notable goalscoring milestone in the process.

Keane Lewis-Potter's deflected effort gives Brentford the lead! ? https://t.co/aN8vIDlT8y

Lewis-Potter's deflected opener will go down in history as Brentford's 300th Premier League goal.

The milestone strike took place over five years after Sergio Canos scored Brentford's first Premier League goal in a 2-0 victory over Arsenal.

Yoane Wissa may have damaged his relationship with Brentford supporters with the manner of his exit to Newcastle United in the summer of 2025, but he played a key role in the Bees hitting the 300-goal mark, considering he is the club's leading Premier League goalscorer with 45 goals in 137 games.

Bryan Mbeumo is in second place on Brentford's all-time Premier League goalscorer list with 42 strikes in 136 matches.

Ivan Toney, meanwhile, scored 36 goals in 83 top-flight appearances for the Bees before he left for Al-Ahli in 2024.

Two current Brentford stars, Igor Thiago and Kevin Shade, will be looking to chase the tallies of the aforementioned trio, having scored 24 Premier League goals apiece in their time with the West London club.

"That is SPECIAL, from Vitaly Janelt!" ? https://t.co/qoSUTWlARb

After claiming their first home win over Everton in three years, Keith Andrews's side have moved up to sixth spot in the Premier League table, with four points separating them from fourth-placed Liverpool.

Brentford will now turn their focus to three high-profile games against Manchester United, Arsenal and Manchester City.

They will travel to Old Trafford this Saturday with hopes of claiming their first-ever Premier League win over Man United, who are reeling from Sunday's heavy 4-0 loss to Liverpool.

#1663. Luca Williams-Barnett signs new Tottenham contract after stellar full debut

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract, tying his long-term future to his boyhood club.

The 18-year-old was in the final two years of his existing contract, but has now agreed fresh terms.

Much has been expected of Williams-Barnett for quite some time, after impressing at both domestic and international youth levels with Spurs and England, and he has had to be patient after being given his senior debut last season in the Carabao Cup aged just 16 years old.

Two short cameos in the Premier League earlier this season led to a first senior start on Saturday for the visit of Ipswich, in which the teenager produced a star performance with a goal and assist in a 2-0 win.

Williams-Barnett became Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 when putting Spurs ahead after just 15 minutes, before turning provider to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half-time.

Reacting to the man-of-the-match performance, which earned the youngster a standing ovation from the home crowd, Roberto De Zerbi compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona star Lamine Yamal.

"I’m positive about that because he has great confidence. He knows all his qualities, but I think he has a very good family and it’s crucial for this type of player," De Zerbi said.

"I think he’s already in a top club. He has nothing to change because he’s already at the top of the level of the club he wants to arrive. He understands because he’s smart. He’s smart to understand the behaviour.

"I think I’m positive about his behaviour, his character, because I’ve been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough to say this."

De Zerbi said: "When I said the first 11 to the players, I said, ‘remember the first game, the debut of you, and help the kid tomorrow, because he’s one of us, and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game.’”

#1662. Liverpool hit with double injury blow for Club Brugge travelling squad confirmed

Andoni Iraola has named his travelling squad for Liverpool’s Champions League trip to Club Brugge, with one notable omission.

Currently in eighth place, the Reds are only ahead of ninth-place Brugge on goals scored and are seeking three points that would allow them to reinforce their position in automatic qualification places.

Key players such as captain Virgil Van Dijk and midfield maestro Dominik Szoboszlai are fit to travel after facing minor injury struggles this season, but one midfielder was not so lucky.

Ryan Gravenberch is not among the 22 who have travelled to Bruges for Wednesday’s fixture, as he continues his recovery from a heel fracture.

The midfielder was a notable absence for Liverpool’s triumphant 4-0 drubbing of rivals Manchester United last week, and remains sidelined while managing pain.

Gravenberch has enjoyed a prolific Reds career since joining in 2023, lifting both the Premier League title and Young Player of the Season award in 2023/24 and penning a new six-year contract this year.

#1661. Lyon vs Lillestrom - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 23 Nov 2026 23:10, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 23:14

Lyon can maintain their perfect home record in Europe this season and potentially climb into the top eight in the Europa League table with a win over Lillestrom on Thursday at Groupama Stadium.

After four matches, Les Gones sit 13th in the table after drawing Real Sociedad 1-1 in Spain, while Lillestrom are 34th following a 1-0 defeat versus Viktoria Plezenn earlier this month.

Olympique Lyonnais are under new management, and it was a successful debut for Carlos Vicens this past weekend, as he won his first match in charge over Lille (1-0).

That snapped a two-match winless run for Les Gones across all competitions, and on Thursday the former Manchester City assistant will coach in his first game with the club at Groupama Stadium.

His team can extend their home winning run across all competitions to six matches this week, netting multiple goals in each of those last five victories.

At the same time, they can win a sixth successive League Phase home outing in this competition as they have not lost a Europa League group match at home since Besiktas beat them 1-0 in 2024.

After four matchdays in the Europa League this season, they are tied with five other teams for that final automatic place in the round of 16 and can end a two-match winless run in this portion of the tournament on Thursday.

Les Gones have never lost a European meeting against a side from Norway, winning their two previous Champions League home games versus Rosenborg this century by a combined margin of 7-1.

The League Phase of this competition has been exceedingly difficult for Lillestrom who, after four matchdays, have just one point.

Hans Erik Odegaard, the father of Arsenal and Norway captain Martin Odegaard, has seen his team concede a combined 10 goals in this phase of the Europa League, while netting only twice.

That said, the Norwegians are in good form domestically, winning five of their last six competitive encounters, all versus teams from Norway.

This week they have a chance to win a Europa League away match for the first time since 2022, when they blanked Finnish side SJK 1-0 in a Conference League qualifying fixture.

Lillestrom have yet to score an opening-half goal in the League Phase of this tournament, with their only two strikes coming beyond the 75th minute.

Kanarifugla can collect their first European victory versus a French opponent this week, having lost their only two competitive visits to France.

Due to a groin strain, Lyon could be missing Tyler Morton for this match, while Mohamed Ouedraogo is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear and Pavel Sulc is doubtful because of a meniscus injury.

Corentin Tolisso scored their equaliser on matchday four, his second in the Europa League this season, while Mads Bidstrup netted his first for the club in Ligue 1 this past weekend and Dominik Greif picked up a clean sheet with five saves.

A groin issue may keep Camil Jebara out for Lillestrom lineup on Thursday, while Espen Garnas is recovering from a knee injury and Lars Mogstad Ranger is questionable with a hip problem.

Thomas Lehne Olsen has the only two goals for them in the League Phase of this competition, with Eric Kitolano and Frederik Elkaer scoring in their 2-0 domestic triumph versus Sarpsborg on Sunday.

Lyon are among the strongest defensive teams in Ligue 1, and against a side lacking much quality in the attacking third at this level.
